subject: science
title: 3D Carbon Bond Builder — Hydrocarbons, Ethanol & Ethanoic Acid
subtitle: Tetravalency, catenation, alkanes/alkenes/alkynes, bromine water test, and –OH / –COOH functional groups
curiosity_hook: Why is Methane (CH₄) a 3D pyramid (109.5°) while Ethene (C₂H₄) is flat and Ethyne (C₂H₂) is a straight line?
source_verified_by: AGY Pass 2 3D Blueprint Build (pending human chemistry teacher sign-off)
learning_objectives: Explore 3D molecular shapes of saturated alkanes (CH₄), unsaturated alkenes (C₂H₄) and alkynes (C₂H₂), and functional-group derivatives (Ethanol, Ethanoic Acid).
Apply general formulas CnH2n+2 (Alkane), CnH2n (Alkene), and CnH2n−2 (Alkyne) and predict the bromine water test result.
Identify functional groups (–OH alcohol in Ethanol, –COOH carboxylic acid in Ethanoic Acid) and compute their molecular masses.

concept_outline.heading: Catenation, Tetravalency & Saturated vs Unsaturated Hydrocarbons (11.2–11.3.1)
concept_outline.summary: Carbon forms 4 covalent bonds and chains with itself (catenation). Alkanes (CnH2n+2) have only C–C single bonds (saturated), whereas Alkenes (C=C, CnH2n) and Alkynes (C≡C, CnH2n−2) are unsaturated.

concept_outline.heading: Bromine Water Test & Reactivity Order (11.3.2)
concept_outline.summary: Unsaturated hydrocarbons (alkenes and alkynes) decolourise reddish-brown bromine water, whereas saturated alkanes do not. Alkynes are the most reactive class due to their triple bond.

concept_outline.heading: Ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH) & Ethanoic Acid (CH₃COOH) (11.6–11.7)
concept_outline.summary: Replacing a hydrogen atom with –OH gives an alcohol (Ethanol, 46 g/mol), while –COOH gives a carboxylic acid (Ethanoic Acid / acetic acid, 60 g/mol, found as 5–8% solution in vinegar).

key_terms.definition: Carbon's unique ability to form strong covalent chains and rings with other carbon atoms.
Hydrocarbon containing only C–C single covalent bonds (CnH2n+2); does not decolourise bromine water.
Hydrocarbon containing at least one C=C double bond (alkene) or C≡C triple bond (alkyne).
An atom or group of atoms (like –OH or –COOH) that determines the characteristic chemical properties of an organic compound.

controls.label: Organic Molecule Switcher
controls.description: Orbit Methane, Ethene, Ethyne, Ethanol, and Ethanoic Acid in 3D.

controls.label: Virtual Bromine Water Test
controls.description: Test whether the selected molecule is saturated or unsaturated.

expected_observations: Methane forms a 3D tetrahedron (109.5°) and does not decolourise bromine water.
Ethene (double bond, 120° planar) and Ethyne (triple bond, 180° linear) both decolourise bromine water.
limitations: Virtual bromine water test is conceptual only — liquid bromine is corrosive and toxic and not handled outside supervised labs.
interaction.safety_note: Conceptual virtual test only. Bromine and concentrated organic chemicals require supervised laboratory fume-hood controls.

storyboard.title: Orbit Tetrahedral Methane (CH₄)
storyboard.learner_action: Rotate CH₄ in 3D to see why its 4 H atoms point to corners of a tetrahedron.
storyboard.expected_response: Bond angle reads 109.5°, saturated alkane (16 g/mol).

storyboard.learner_action: Switch to Ethene (C₂H₄) and Ethyne (C₂H₂) and click Run Test.
storyboard.expected_response: Double/triple cylinders render between C1–C2 and bromine water decolourises.

storyboard.title: Inspect –OH and –COOH Groups
storyboard.learner_action: Select Ethanol and Ethanoic Acid and click the red Oxygen atoms.
storyboard.expected_response: Highlights hydroxyl (–OH, 46 g/mol) vs carboxyl (–COOH, 60 g/mol).

steps.heading: Alkanes (CnH2n+2)
steps.description: Single C–C bonds only; saturated; least reactive.
steps.key_takeaway: Methane CH₄, Ethane C₂H₆, Propane C₃H₈.

steps.heading: Alkenes (CnH2n) & Alkynes (CnH2n−2)
steps.description: Contain C=C double or C≡C triple bonds; unsaturated; decolourise bromine water.

steps.heading: Functional Groups (–OH & –COOH)
steps.description: Ethanol ends in -ol (–OH); Ethanoic acid ends in -oic acid (–COOH).
steps.key_takeaway: Functional groups control chemical reactions and IUPAC suffixes.

question_bank.prompt: Which general formula represents the Alkene homologous series (containing a C=C double bond)?

options.label: CnH2n+2
options.feedback: CnH2n+2 is the saturated Alkane series.

options.label: CnH2n
options.feedback: Correct! For n = 2, C₂H₄ is Ethene; for n = 3, C₃H₆ is Propene.

options.label: CnH2n−2
options.feedback: CnH2n−2 is the Alkyne series (triple bond).

options.label: CnH2n+1OH
options.feedback: That is the alcohol homologous series.

question_bank.worked_explanation: Alkenes have one C=C double bond, reducing hydrogen count by 2 compared to alkanes → CnH2n.

question_bank.prompt: A hydrocarbon sample rapidly decolourises reddish-brown bromine water. What does this confirm (p. 158)?

options.label: It is a saturated alkane
options.feedback: Saturated alkanes do NOT decolourise bromine water.

options.label: It is an unsaturated hydrocarbon (alkene or alkyne)
options.feedback: Correct! Double or triple bonds react with bromine, discharging its colour.

options.label: It is pure water
options.feedback: Water does not decolourise bromine water.

options.label: It has no carbon atoms
options.feedback: All hydrocarbons contain carbon and hydrogen.

question_bank.worked_explanation: Unsaturated bonds (C=C or C≡C) undergo addition with bromine, decolourising bromine water.

question_bank.prompt: What is the molecular mass and functional group of Ethanoic Acid (CH₃COOH)?
question_bank.hint: Count 2 C, 4 H, 2 O using C=12, H=1, O=16.
question_bank.worked_explanation: CH₃COOH has 2 C (24) + 4 H (4) + 2 O (32) = 60 g/mol and carries the –COOH carboxylic acid group.

worked_feedback: Always verify carbon's tetravalency (4 bonds per carbon) in every structural formula.
Compare single, double, and triple bonds visually in 3D to remember geometry: 109.5° → 120° → 180°.

flashcards.front: General formulas of Alkane, Alkene, Alkyne
flashcards.back: Alkane: CnH2n+2; Alkene: CnH2n; Alkyne: CnH2n−2.
Unsaturated compounds (C=C, C≡C) decolourise bromine water; saturated alkanes do not.

flashcards.front: Functional groups of Ethanol vs Ethanoic Acid
flashcards.back: Ethanol: –OH (alcohol, 46 g/mol); Ethanoic Acid: –COOH (carboxylic acid, 60 g/mol).
